newsitem.title: USA: Hillenbrand sees European health care losses.
newsitem.headline: Hillenbrand sees European health care losses.

text.p: Hillenbrand Industries Inc said Tuesday it expects losses in its health care businesses in certain European countries, especially France and Germany, to continue through the balance of fiscal 1996.
Mark Craft, a spokesman, said the losses from the European health care businesses may also continue into fiscal 1997.

While there is good underlying demand for products such as hospital furniture in Europe, the health care segment is being hurt by governmental budget constraints and economic conditions in certain countries, Hillenbrand said.
Craft said that Hillenbrand hopes to be profitable in Germany in 1997.
"We continue to hold our own," he said, adding the European business is benefiting from restructuring.

Earlier, Hillenbrand reported earnings for the third quarter ended August 31 of $0.50 a share compared with $0.37 a year ago. Excluding extraordinary items, including a gain on the sale of Block Medical, Hillenbrand's third quarter operating earnings were $0.45 a share, Craft said.
Third quarter operating profit in the health care segment grew at double-digit rates due to higher domestic volume, a shift in sales mix to higher-margin products and cost controls.

The company said it was encouraged by the strong domestic capital sales at the Hill-Rom division. This improvement was offset by lower European sales that carry lower margins, the disposition of Block Medical in July and lower sales at its Medeco business.
Hillenbrand said its funeral services segment reported good growth in revenues and operating profit.
